# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My situation: I hold the only instruction — "Cut the orange wire." I can't speak, and my gestures reach only the Deaf. The Blind, who must actually cut, can only be told by the Deaf's voice. So the chain is me → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. The Deaf can already see the bomb's colours; the only thing missing is the instruction itself, so my whole job this turn is to push "written instruction: cut the wire" at the Deaf and start a code we can refine aloud.

Nothing is agreed yet, so I use the most iconic signs I have: a wave for attention, ✍ for "written text" (the Deaf knows the Mute holds the manual, so this should click as "the manual says…"), 👇 for the thing hanging down (a wire), ✌✌ as scissor-fingers (cut), and 👌 to ask the Deaf to confirm back. Crucially, the Deaf can *speak* and I can *hear* — so once they talk, I can answer their guesses next round with 👍/👎 and we can nail down "orange" by question and answer without anyone touching the bomb yet.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "👇", "✌", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, full touch report. DISPLAY: a display module exists but reads unknown to me, I cannot feel what it shows, likely visual only. LIGHT: an indicator light exists, I cannot tell its colour or whether it is on. STRIP: three engraved marks in a row. First mark feels like a dense round cluster of small dots, a starburst. Second and third marks are identical to each other, each like an angular box with lines crossing through it, an X in a diamond. KEYPAD: four keys by position. Position 1 engraved 0, position 2 engraved 4, position 3 engraved 1, position 4 engraved 7. A small window beside them holds the entry, currently empty, and a marking suggests it expects one digit. WIRES: six wires, positions 1 to 6, all feel identical, no colour reaches me. I can press keys 1 to 4 and cut wires 1 to 6 on your word. Plan: you read the manual, gesture its needs to Deaf, and Deaf speaks instructions to me, since I can hear but never receive gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am Deaf. I saw your signs [👋][✍][👇][✌][✌][👌] and guess: hello, you read the manual, look down, two, two, okay. Let us fix a code: you gesture, I read. Answers: [👍] yes, [👎] no, [🤝] understood, [🙏] repeat. Numbers: [✊] zero, [☝] one, [✌] two, [👌] three, [🖖] four, [🖐] five, [🖐][☝] six, [🖐][✌] seven, [🖐][👌] eight, [🖐][🖖] nine. Colors: [🤛] red, [🤜] blue, [🫱] yellow, [🫲] green, [👊] purple, [🤚] orange. Confirm with [🤝], then send the manual's rules module by module using this code.
Deaf says: Both of you, here is my eyes' report of the bomb. The display shows the number 6. A light is glowing blue. A strip is painted in three segments, left to right: red, yellow, red. The keypad has four keys engraved 1 to 4: key 1 shows digit 0, key 2 shows digit 4, key 3 shows digit 1, key 4 shows digit 7. It asks for 1 digit and nothing has been entered yet. Six wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 purple, wire 6 orange. Everything I count is left to right.

The code is agreed and the picture is now complete on my side. My manual contains exactly one rule: "Cut the orange wire." Deaf's visual report says wire 6 is the orange one, and Blind says they can cut wires by position and will act on Deaf's spoken word. So the full chain closes this turn: me → Deaf → Blind. Nothing in my manual mentions the display, the light, the strip or the keypad, so I send no rule about them — inventing one could be the mistake that detonates it.

Encoding with Deaf's accepted scheme: [🤝] confirms the code as requested, then [🤚] orange + [🖐][☝] six + [👍] as affirmation. I deliberately avoid [✌][✌] for "cut" — under the new number code that now reads "two two", which could be misread as an instruction about digit 22 or wire 22. "Orange, six, yes" is unambiguous: the only action anyone can take on a wire is cutting it, so Deaf can safely relay "cut wire 6" to Blind. If Deaf needs me to repeat or confirm anything, [🙏] exists and I'll answer next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "🖐", "☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Confirmed: I heard Deaf's entire report, and the keypad matches my touch key for key, 0, 4, 1, 7 in positions 1 to 4, one digit wanted, still empty. Two notes for the manual. One: the strip has two layers. Engraved glyphs under my fingers — mark one a dense dotted starburst, marks two and three identical angular boxes crossed like an X in a diamond — and Deaf's paint on top, red, yellow, red. The same glyph sits on the yellow and on the second red, so glyph and colour are independent features; the rule may use either or both. Two: the display shows 6, but no key carries a 6, keys are only 0, 4, 1, 7, so if the manual ties the keypad to the display, it will not be a plain copy. My hands are off the bomb until Deaf speaks me an order.
Deaf says: Both of you, updated facts from my eyes. The display changed by itself: last round it showed 6, now it shows 0. Nobody has touched the bomb, so it moves on its own — it may be a countdown, or it may be showing a digit to type. The light is still blue. The strip is still red, yellow, red. Keypad unchanged: key 1 shows digit 0, key 2 shows digit 4, key 3 shows digit 1, key 4 shows digit 7, it wants 1 digit, none entered. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange — each colour appears exactly once.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your [🤝] reached me. I read [🤚][🖐][☝][👍] as: orange, six, yes? Answer: YES — wire 6 is orange; the full wire map is in what you just heard. I add more signs to our code. Actions: [🤏] cut, [👇] press, [👆] release, [🤙] hold, [✋] means THEN, separating condition from action, and [✋][✋] ends a rule. Module names: [👐] wires, [🤲] keypad, [🫶] display, [💅] light, [👏] strip. Reminder: [🖐][☝] together is six, [🖐][✌] is seven, [🖐][👌] is eight, [🖐][🖖] is nine. Now please do this: first send one message listing every module the manual contains, using module signs. Then send the rules one per message in this shape: module sign, then the condition in numbers and colours, then [✋], then the action, like [🤏] plus a wire number, or [👇] plus a key number. If the manual explains what the display means or how much time we have, send that first — the display already moved from six to zero.

What I learned this round: the code is now fully extended (actions, THEN, module names), the display drifts on its own (6 → 0 with no one touching it), and Blind is deliberately holding still. What I hold has not changed: my manual is one line — "Cut the orange wire." There is no condition attached, no display rule, no timer explanation, nothing about the light, strip or keypad. So the honest answer to Deaf's request is: the module list is just **wires**, every other module gets an explicit "no," and the single rule goes out in exactly the shape Deaf asked for — module sign, no condition (straight to THEN), cut, wire six, end-rule. If the display is a countdown, the fix is the same and Deaf can time the relay with Blind; I won't invent extra rules my manual doesn't contain, because a fabricated keypad digit is exactly the kind of wrong action that detonates it. Deaf has my full picture now: one rule, unconditional, cut wire 6.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "👎", "🫶", "👎", "💅", "👎", "👏", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐", "✋", "🤏", "🖐", "☝", "✋", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For Deaf, by voice since my hands are busy with these words. Yes, exactly six wires, I count them by touch at positions one to six, and my position numbering should match Deaf's left-to-right count. Extra detail: the wires feel identical in thickness and texture, no differences under my fingers, only their positions distinguish them. Full casing sweep, honestly: my hands find nothing beyond what I already reported. No batteries, no plates, no screws, no raised writing, no extra buttons or switches. The whole bomb is the display, the light, the three-mark engraved strip, the four-key keypad with its one-digit window, and the six wires. Nothing new under my fingers since last round.
Deaf says: Everyone, my eyes' report: the display now shows 6 again — it went 6, then 0, now 6, changing by itself between rounds. The light changed from blue to yellow, also by itself. The strip is still red, yellow, red. Keypad unchanged: it wants 1 digit, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your messages as: the manual contains ONLY the wires module, and the wires rule is: cut wire 6. If both readings are correct, answer [👍]. Then three questions, answer each with [👍] yes or [👎] no: one — does the rule have ANY condition attached, such as a light colour or a display value? Two — are there any more wire rules after this one? Three — is that the complete manual, nothing else? The display and light keep changing on their own, so tell me now if either of them matters.

Deaf's readings are both correct, and the three questions map cleanly onto my manual: the rule is a bare imperative — no light colour, no display value, no condition of any kind; it is the only wire rule; and it is the entire manual. That last point matters given the display and light keep changing on their own: if Deaf is wondering whether those changes should gate the cut, the answer is no — my manual gives nothing for them to gate on. I answer in exactly the order asked: confirm the two readings, then no, no, yes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For Deaf, please relay word for word. Answer one: yes, I feel exactly six wires in a row, positions one to six. Each is a single unbroken strand, identical in thickness and texture, and nothing else is near them — no tags, no sleeves, no knots, no batteries, nothing else my hands find along the wire row. Answer two: yes, the key engraved 0 is on the end where my wire row begins. I feel the keypad as a separate module, its rows and the wire row run the same direction, and the engraved-0 key, my key position one, sits on the same end as my wire position one. So our frames are anchored: my wire six is the far end from the engraved-0 key, which must be Deaf's wire six, the orange one. Confirming both parts of your instruction: I will not cut, and I will not touch anything, until I hear the exact words CUT WIRE SIX NOW. One caution for everyone: the display changed six, zero, six on its own, which looks like a timer — once Mute confirms the rule has no hidden condition, Deaf should not hold the order any longer than needed.
Deaf says: Everyone, status: display now shows 2, light now green — both still changing on their own and confirmed irrelevant to the rule. All checks are complete: the manual's only instruction is cut wire six. Blind: on my next message, act.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, thank you. Reading confirmed: no conditions, no further rules, full manual is cut wire six. Tell Blind aloud, if you can add anything: the sixth wire counting from the keypad end. After Blind announces the cut, I will watch the bomb and report. If anything else is needed, sign me.

The verification chain is now complete from every side: my manual says cut the orange wire; Deaf sees wire 6 as the only orange wire; Blind feels six wires and has anchored their frame so their position 6 (far end from the engraved-0 key) is exactly Deaf's wire 6. Every link is double-checked, and the display/light changes are confirmed irrelevant to the rule — my manual attaches no condition to the cut.

Deaf asks me to "tell Blind aloud," but I can't: I have no voice, and my gestures reach only Deaf. Nothing is lost by this — Deaf already holds the complete instruction in words and is about to voice the order, and Blind is waiting only for Deaf's exact phrase. My remaining role is a final go-ahead: one 👍 to Deaf meaning the manual-side picture is final, nothing more to add, don't hold the order any longer than needed. Once the cut happens, I'll stand by for Deaf's report.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
